inputs.share_count_basis: 2,415,170,102 ordinary shares at 17 Sep 2026 (FY2026 AR shareholder information): 2,325,170,102 at 30 Jun 2026 plus 90,000,000 ATM shares issued to Acuity Capital on 13 Aug 2026. 478,136,676 LKEO listed options (A$0.05, exp 14 Oct 2028) are out of the money and excluded, except that any scenario worth more than A$0.05 a share is diluted for their exercise (cash in, shares out). EXCLUDED: 4.98m unlisted options (A$0.21-1.13), 102.9m PSUs with share-price hurdles of A$0.325 and up (they would add ~4% in the bull case only), ~0.9m RSUs. Funding dilution is NOT put through the count: pre-FID burn is deducted in USD and construction equity is charged as a dilution cost in each scenario bridge. Any shares issued after 17 Sep 2026 are not in the count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Pro-forma cash A$11.57m: A$6.668m at 30 Jun 2026 plus A$4.9m of ATM proceeds received July-August 2026, matched to the 2,415m share count. No borrowings; lease liabilities A$0.5m ignored. At the FY2026 burn (~A$21m a year) roughly A$7-8m of this has been spent by the valuation date; that spend is charged in the scenarios as pre-FID burn from the balance date, not netted here.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2026: OCF -17.469, capitalised exploration and evaluation plus PP&E -3.465, less SBC and interest income. Not a base for projection; it is the pre-FID burn rate.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report income statement, share-based payments expense 6,105,520 (note 20)
inputs.fx_note: Statements and quote are both AUD. The Kachi project is modelled in USD (study currency) and translated at AUDUSD 0.6774 (Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 13 Nov 2026). Fields suffixed _usd_m are US$ millions; everything else is A$.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T05:12:02Z regular ASX close (Yahoo regularMarketTime); a 52-week low

project_anchors.study: Kachi Phase One DFS Addendum, August 2025 (Hatch)
project_anchors.provenance: NPV, IRR, price deck, capex, opex, reserve, first-year tonnes and Lilac's interest are read from the FY2026 annual report. NOT in the extracted filings and therefore assumed: a three-year build spent 30/45/25%, a 25% RIGI income-tax rate and a 3% provincial royalty for the price sensitivity, and whether the study NPV is stated at 100% of the project (assumed 100%). The steady-state after-tax cash flow is solved so the model reproduces the disclosed post-tax NPV10; as a cross-check, price less opex on 25,000 t is US$365m pre-tax and the same shape gives a pre-tax NPV10 close to the disclosed US$1,469m.

inputs.wacc_rationale: USD project flows, USD rate, unlevered. US 10-year ~4.3% + 5% ERP x asset beta ~1.2 gives ~10%; base adds one point for Argentina and a first-of-scale DLE flowsheet (11%), bull uses 10%, the study's own rate. Risk is otherwise charged in the flows (price below the study deck, capex and opex overruns, slower ramp), in the financing discount, and in the scenario weights, not stacked again in the rate.
inputs.nci_treatment: Lilac Solutions holds 20% of Kachi Lithium Pty Ltd and earns a further 5% on Tier 1 product qualification, which any financed project will have achieved. Proceed scenarios take 75% of project NPV and 75% of the funding obligation; the bear residual is taken on consolidated book, which slightly flatters it.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: risked-project-npv. Pre-revenue single-asset developer with a going-concern material uncertainty; dcf-methods SKILL.md has no routing row for it, and the folder precedent for an UNBUILT project (INR.AX, SMI.NZ) is a risked project NPV written directly as JSON, not the owner-FCF engine (no revenue, every historical cash flow is study spend funded by issuance). Not routed to the distressed waterfall either: the company is solvent, debt-free and holds a permitted asset. Structure: bear = no financing, value is a fraction of capitalised project spend plus cash less holding costs; base and bull = Kachi reaches FID, valued as LKE's 75% of a re-cut study NPV less the cost of raising construction equity at a discount through a company worth about US$40m. FINDING: on base terms (US$18,000/t, 11%, +15% capex, new equity at a 30% discount) the dilution cost is about equal to LKE's whole share of project NPV, so base is floored at the stalled-asset value and equals bear. Value above that floor comes only from the bull case. Historical CAGRs set no driver. Multiples sanity checks do not apply; price is 0.42x book (NTA A$0.057 a share).

historical_growth.notes: Pre-revenue developer: no revenue or positive FCF in any of 22 periods, EPS negative throughout. Equity moved only with issuance and write-offs (A$46.9m FY2021, A$218.8m FY2022, A$137.7m FY2026) while shares on issue went from 822m to 2,415m. Owner FCF (after SBC and interest) FY2023-FY2026: -111.4, -88.1, -35.1, -27.4. All CAGRs deliberately null.

base.scenario: Partner signed during 2027, FID mid-2028, first production 2031. LCE US$18,000/t (bottom of the current spot range, 12% under the study deck), capex 15% and opex 10% over the DFS Addendum, 60%/90% ramp. Lilac at 25%. Project financed 55% debt; LKE's equity share raised at a 30% discount to intrinsic value.
base.terminal_note: Finite 25-year reserve life in closed form; no terminal value and no credit for the 11.1 Mt resource beyond the 0.63 Mt reserve.

bull.scenario: Strategic or ECA-backed partner in the first half of 2027 entering near intrinsic value (15% discount), FID late 2027. LCE US$22,000/t, capex and opex on the DFS Addendum, 60% debt.
bull.terminal_note: Finite 25-year reserve life in closed form; no terminal value and no credit for the 11.1 Mt resource beyond the 0.63 Mt reserve.

bear.scenario: No partner and no FID inside three years; the company keeps the tenements and permits alive on small ATM raises at a cut-down cost base.
bear.components_note: 30% of the A$136.8m capitalised exploration and evaluation asset (US$27.8m, about US$3 per tonne of attributable resource LCE: a permitted, DFS-stage brine deposit keeps option value unfunded) plus pro-forma cash, less three years of holding costs at US$8m a year, roughly 60% of the FY2026 burn. Not zero, and not discounted.

projections.note: Closed-form project model at 100% of Kachi, US$m, years counted from FID. Construction years 1-3 take 30/45/25% of capex; production year 1 runs at 60%, year 2 at 90%, then steady state to the end of a 25-year reserve life. revenue is LCE price x tonnes.

bear.note: No project cash flows; asset and cash residual only.

base.floor_note: Financing on these terms costs existing holders more than their share of the project NPV (unfloored equity at FID is negative). Holders would not approve it; the scenario value is the stalled-asset value used in the bear case, i.e. Kachi is worth more to them sold or held than financed.

entry_price.method_note: No terminal value, so the standard TV-at-hurdle formula does not apply. The price that clears 15% a year to first production (years to FID plus a three-year build) is IV x ((1+r)/1.15)^n. Bear, and base because it sits on the same floor, use three years at 11%.

required_return_table.note: Base-scenario proceed value, A$ per share, at alternative unlevered discount rates, funding structure held constant, floored at zero rather than at the stalled-asset value. Not weighted for financing risk.

sensitivity.axes_note: Rows = long-run lithium carbonate price (US$/t LCE), columns = unlevered discount rate (%). Base-scenario structure (capex +15%, opex +10%, 30% new-money discount), A$ per share, NOT weighted for financing risk. Terminal growth does not exist in this model; lithium price replaces it. Cells are floored at zero: a zero means the project cannot be financed on those terms without wiping out existing holders, and the realistic outcome there is the stalled-asset value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Framed on the financing binary, not on growth. Kachi financed on terms that leave existing holders materially better off than the stalled asset: 6%. Financed on ordinary terms: 22%. Not financed inside three years: 72%. For a financing: the DIA was granted in September 2026, lithium carbonate has recovered to US$18-20,000/t, RIGI offers 30-year fiscal stability, and Rio Tinto and others are committing capital to neighbouring salars. Against: the Goldman Sachs-led partner process has run for years without an equity partner or a binding offtake; LKE's share of construction equity is roughly twelve times its market value; DLE is unproven at 25,000 tpa; the auditor flags a going-concern uncertainty; and the share price reached a 52-week low after the approval, on the way to another raise. Bull is held at 6% because it needs a price above the study deck, an on-budget first-of-scale build and a partner paying near intrinsic value, together.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street bases coincide (no SBC adjustment in a project NPV); the band collapsed.
probability_weighted.market_implied_note: Holding the base:bull mix at 22:6, the current price is what the model returns at this combined probability of a financing, against the 28% used here. Because base sits on the floor, this is equivalent to a bull-case probability of about 4.9% against the 6% used.

scenario_narratives.base: A partner signs in 2027 and FID follows in mid-2028. At US$18,000/t and 11% the whole project is worth about US$282m at FID and LKE's 75% about US$212m, but LKE's share of construction equity is about US$494m, and raising that at a 30% discount costs existing holders about US$212m. Nothing is left over: success on ordinary terms is worth no more to today's holders than the unfunded asset, so the scenario is valued at that floor.
scenario_narratives.bull: A strategic or export-credit-backed investor enters near intrinsic value in the first half of 2027, lithium holds US$22,000/t and the build comes in on the DFS Addendum. Project NPV at FID is about US$1104m at 10%, LKE's share US$828m, and the dilution cost falls to about US$67m. Essentially all of the value above the floor sits here.
scenario_narratives.bear: No binding partner and no FID inside three years. The company keeps the permits alive on small raises. Value is 30% of capitalised project spend plus cash less holding costs.

valuation_philosophy.approach: Risked project NPV for a pre-revenue, single-asset lithium brine developer
valuation_philosophy.summary: Lake is a claim on one unbuilt project that needs about US$1.2-1.3bn, held through a company worth about US$40m with a few months of cash. The study's US$1.0bn post-tax NPV is a 10% value of the whole project at US$20,500/t before anyone pays for it; existing holders own 75% of that, re-cut at a lower price and a higher cost, less what it costs to bring in roughly US$400-500m of new equity. On ordinary terms that subtraction leaves nothing above what the asset is worth unfunded. The stock is therefore an option on a narrow combination - strong lithium, an on-budget build and a partner who pays near intrinsic value - and the weighted value is the price of that option plus a small asset floor, not a central estimate.
key_risks_to_valuation: The weighted value is dominated by a 6% bull weight: each point of bull probability is worth about A$0.0034 a share, 14% of the current price
New-money discount: in the base structure every 10 points is worth more than LKE's whole share of project NPV
Near-term raise: cash covers a few months; shares issued after 17 Sep 2026 at these prices are not in the count and would lower every per-share value
Lithium price: the study deck is US$20,500/t; the base structure leaves holders nothing at or below about US$18,000/t at 11%
Study inputs not in the extracted filings (construction phasing, tax rate, royalty, whether NPV is at 100%) are assumptions; if the study NPV is already LKE's share, proceed values rise by a third
Bear residual (30% of book, ~US$3/t LCE attributable) is a judgment; a distressed sale or a tenement lapse would realise less, a strategic bid for an 11 Mt permitted resource could realise much more
DLE at 25,000 tpa is unproven; the 60%/90% ramp and +10% opex in base may be too kind
No evidence after the FY2026 annual report and the September 2026 DIA was available in the extracted filings; the September quarterly cash balance should replace the pro-forma figure
